title: Musk's Public Backing of $3.5T SpaceX-Tesla Merger Rattles Insiders, Threatens Weeks of Delay

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Elon Musk's public endorsement of a potential $3.5 trillion merger between SpaceX and Tesla has rattled insiders involved in the talks, who warn his remarks could Delay negotiations by several weeks and invite shareholder legal challenges, Reuters reported. Insiders noted that Musk is barred from the discussions due to conflicts of interest and fear a repeat of the litigation over Tesla's SolarCity acquisition, which ended in a $60 million settlement by directors. Tesla shares fell 3.7% in premarket trading Thursday as the automaker formally confirmed its special committee is exploring arrangements with SpaceX, including a combination.

SpaceX approached Tesla in recent weeks, with the companies weighing either a SpaceX takeover or an all stock merger under a new holding company. A tie up would also face national security and data sharing scrutiny from regulators in both the US and China, given SpaceX's role as a Pentagon contractor and Tesla's manufacturing footprint in China.

The push to combine the $2 trillion rocket maker and $1.5 trillion automaker centers on artificial intelligence, with SpaceX's data centers and satellite links serving as infrastructure for Tesla's robotaxis and Optimus robots. SpaceX's AI unit has become its largest business, generating $7.56 billion in third quarter revenue compared with $813 million a year earlier and accounting for more than $16.4 billion of its $19.6 billion in quarterly capital spending. Advisers to Musk have aimed to announce an agreement in the first half of 2027 to close the deal before the end of President Donald Trump's term.

selectedTweets.text:
Elon Musk explains where a SpaceX–Tesla merger stands:

“I mean, this is definitely kind of a question where I feel like I’m tap dancing through a minefield. But so I have to be thoughtful about what I say here."

"I think so both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss this idea at the request of shareholders. And these special committees consist of independent directors. And because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions of the special committees."

"So it’s sort of a, it’s an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking and I can’t be in the conversation."

"I mean, I don’t think we should necessarily assume that it’s, I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it."

"The, you know, do I think it would be a good idea? Yes. But at the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this, and particularly on the Tesla side, we will need a 50 percent vote of all shares, not just those who vote, but of all shareholders. And that’s quite a high hurdle to try to achieve."

"So and I can just say at this point that the special committees have not reached agreement on the terms of any transaction. And obviously there’s no guarantee that they will."

"But I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity. And there’s a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the TeraFab, obviously, robotics, mass to orbit with the Starmind constellation. Connectivity."

"So, I think it would be a good idea, but it’s really up to the special committees of both companies. Like, they’ve got to come up with something and then that’s got to be put to the shareholders as a vote.”

selectedTweets.text:
WSJ: Musk wants to combine a $2T rocket company with a $1.5T carmaker around AI.

SpaceX’s AI unit is now its largest business, with third-quarter revenue of $7.56B against $813M a year earlier, and more than $16.4B of its $19.6B quarterly capital spending went to AI.

That growth turned SpaceX to a $4.4B quarterly profit from a $1.05B loss, giving it the financial weight to absorb Tesla rather than the reverse.

The AI case for the merger treats Tesla’s robotaxis and Optimus robots as the front end and SpaceX’s data centers and satellite links as the infrastructure they would depend on.
